inspection_outcome: Confirmed core norm-theorem error and invalid published matched-parameter rationale; separate release discrepancy and historical-run limits

findings.title: Non-collinearity and task heterogeneity do not imply unequal gradient norms
findings.confidence: Confirmed analytic counterexample with independently checked model realization
findings.claim: At least one transformer layer must have different norms of the two task-expected gradients.

counterexample.tasks: Same fixed multimodal input; next-token probabilities q_A=(1/2,1/3,1/6) and q_B=(1/3,1/2,1/6).
counterexample.finite_optima: w=log(q)+c*1; task-optimal predictive distributions differ, so no common optimal configuration.
counterexample.checkpoint: At w=0, the expected gradients are g_A=(-1/6,0,1/6) and g_B=(0,-1/6,1/6).
counterexample.assumptions: Distinct distributions and disjoint optimum sets satisfy K.2; no real scalar maps g_B to g_A, satisfying K.3.
counterexample.contradiction: Both squared norms equal 1/18. An active transformer FFN projection has exactly these flattened gradients, and every other layer has zero gradient for both tasks.
counterexample.model_realization: Bias-free residual transformer with fixed hidden activation u=e1, active output projection P=0 and fixed readout w=P u; other branch factors zero and visual-to-predictive projector zero. Finite optima are realized by P u=log(q).
counterexample.sequential_safeguard: A positive-step task-A update can reach w=0 from a finite fixed point w_pre=eta(softmax(w_pre)-q_A); no convergence assumption in the source excludes this.
counterexample.additional_check: g_A^T g_B=1/36>0 and cosine=1/2. Small descent updates improve both task risks, so opposing directions do not follow.

findings.proof_failure: Eq26's equal-length distinct vectors on a sphere are consistent with the assumptions; sequential presentation supplies no contradictory magnitude constraint.
findings.strongest_alternative: A statement that gradient vectors differ is true under K.3 but materially weaker. A trajectory-specific or converged-state theorem would need new quantified assumptions.
findings.impact: Refutes the claimed formal foundation for task-dependent gradient-magnitude discrepancies and the asserted theoretical allocation motivation. Does not refute measured sensitivity patterns, benchmark scores or all practical uses.
findings.repair: Remove/weaken the universal norm theorem or add substantive magnitude assumptions and prove a new statement. Vector-direction discrepancy alone does not imply unequal norms or layer-ranking changes.

findings.confirmed: Under the stated attention-only targets, rank 4 on all blocks gives 1,572,864 weights; Figure 6's task-1 rank-8 allocation gives 1,638,400–1,900,544 regardless of subslot orientation. Count budgets ignore unequal matrix costs.
findings.status: Demonstrated failure of a core matched-parameter rationale; historical-run equality and score effects remain Needs Evidence
findings.strongest_counterevidence: The released baseline wrapper includes FFN targets beyond the manuscript description. Table 11's nominal 2x/4x O-LoRA still scores lower.
findings.not_established: Actual original checkpoint counts, whether the executed comparison favored D-MoLE, or its effect on rankings.
findings.confidence: Confirmed internal mathematical accounting inconsistency under the paper's stated target matrices; historical experiment counts unresolved
findings.claim: Appendix A p.15 states equal trainable parameters for a fair comparison, justified by rank 4 on all baseline locations versus rank 8 with allocation budget ratio 0.5.
findings.operative_assumptions: Use the stated attention/output targets, ranks 4 and 8, 24-layer LLM and vision components, respective model matrix shapes, and the published task-1 Figure 6 selection. This is a test of the published design rationale, not a reconstruction of historical checkpoints.
findings.dependency: The paper uses equal trainable parameter counts to justify the fairness of its central parameter-constrained comparison. Counting selected locations ignores unequal adapter costs and does not establish that claimed control; the published allocation directly violates the equality under the stated architecture.
findings.severity_boundary: Major applies to the demonstrated invalid equality rationale and its core comparison dependency. It does not assert a false score, an executed unfair run, or that budget differences explain the observed advantage.
findings.repair: Replace count-only budgeting with explicit r*(d_in+d_out) costs, reconcile target-module descriptions, and report actual per-task checkpoint tensor counts. Any corrected architecture requires a new matched-budget comparison; no author-adopted or empirical repair is claimed.

confirmed_discrepancies_with_unresolved_.topic: Per-sample top-two versus shared batch-vote routing
confirmed_discrepancies_with_unresolved_.confirmed: The pinned get_task_ids selects one eligible winner per sample, votes across the batch and applies one common mask. A single sample cannot select two experts; an unknown sample can inherit a neighboring sample's expert.
confirmed_discrepancies_with_unresolved_.status: Confirmed release/manuscript discrepancy; Table 2 impact Needs Evidence
confirmed_discrepancies_with_unresolved_.strongest_counterevidence: The current public source is not verified as the exact original experiment revision. No reference-answer or explicit task-label leakage was found in traced main evaluation paths.
confirmed_discrepancies_with_unresolved_.not_established: Numerical effect on original scores or any ranking reversal.

local_corrections_and_scope.status: 15.08, 20.14 and 19.82 are mixed-aggregate score-point differences, not relative percentages; the displayed advantage survives.
Some totals exceed the rounding allowance. Overhead ratios reconstruct and the broad ordering is not refuted.
Removes allocation and routing together; an isolated allocation benefit requires additional evidence.
Empty candidates / all reject is consistent with Eq. (10); the p. 6 any-rejection prose is locally inconsistent.
No independent repeat or uncertainty replication; results remain scoped to the reported model and tasks.

acceptance_calibration.note: D1 receives Major for the demonstrated published equality rationale, separately from unknown historical experiment counts; no empirical-score deterioration is required.
